rows: Work with abrasive wheels should be organised under the general requirements for safe work equipment.
Wheel characteristics must be suitable for the machine, material and operation.
People mounting abrasive wheels need appropriate training and competence.
Before mounting, wheels should be checked for damage and correct specification.
Wheel speed markings must be compatible with the machine spindle speed.
Guards should be correctly fitted and maintained during grinding operations.
Portable and hand-held grinders require controls appropriate to their mobility and use.
Suitable eye, face and other personal protection may be needed for residual risks.
A wheel label or training certificate does not prove that a particular setup is safe.
Task conclusions require wheel condition, speed, mounting, guard, machine, material, operator and PPE evidence.
Work at height should be assessed, organised and planned so it is carried out safely.
General access scaffolds can provide collective fall protection where practicable.
Scaffolds must be designed, erected, altered and dismantled by competent people.
Scaffolding work should be directed by a competent supervisor.
Guard rails, toe boards and other barriers should prevent falls of people and materials.
Some scaffold configurations require a bespoke design rather than a standard arrangement.
Scaffold loading and ties must reflect the intended use and site conditions.
Scaffolds require inspection and defects must be corrected before unsafe use continues.
A scaffold tag does not replace the legally required inspection and report.
Site conclusions require design, erection, ties, foundations, loading, access, inspection and weather evidence.
A tower scaffold should be suitable for the work being carried out.
Towers should be erected and dismantled by trained and competent people.
Users need training in the hazards and precautions associated with tower scaffolds.
Stability depends on the manufacturer's configuration, dimensions and stabilising arrangements.
Platforms should have suitable guard rails and toe boards.
Access should be by the designed internal route rather than climbing the outside.
Towers should be inspected through a rigorous inspection arrangement.
Movement and use should follow the manufacturer's instructions and site controls.
A tower's product standard or inspection label does not prove safe use at a specific location.
Use conclusions require configuration, height, outriggers, ground, access, loading, wind and inspection evidence.
Danger to workers in or near excavations must be prevented.
Ground cannot be assumed to remain stable without support in all circumstances.
Temporary support or safe battering should be planned before excavation starts.
Plant, vehicles and spoil should be kept far enough from excavation edges.
Substantial barriers should prevent people or plant falling into excavations.
Safe access and egress must be provided.
Underground services, water inflow and nearby structures must be considered during planning.
A competent person should inspect excavations at the start of each shift and after relevant events.
An excavation depth or soil description alone does not establish stability.
Safety conclusions require ground, support, water, surcharge, services, access, inspection and weather evidence.
